title: Cornell Flock policy implementation and access-control evidence prerequisites
summary: Official Cornell policy and security-system standards narrow the records needed to prove whether the reported seven-reader Flock deployment was integrated into Cornell's centralized security-video regime: integration or exemption state, authorization/activation forms, NVSSO training/designation, commissioning records, video-management-system instances, and Access Control Program configuration. The sources do not themselves prove that Flock followed that path.

sources.title: 281316 — Electronic Safety and Security Systems
sources.publisher: Cornell University Facilities and Campus Services

caveats: Cornell's 2023 Design and Construction Standard is an official university standard, but this pass does not establish that it governed the reported October 2024 Flock deployment or that Flock readers were commissioned as centralized video-management-system devices.
Policy 8.1 requires centralized integration unless an exemption applies, but the Flock-specific integration or exemption record has not been recovered.
University policy roles and commissioning requirements do not prove that any named person held Flock credentials or performed a query.

data.question: Which Cornell-native implementation records would prove or disprove that the reported Flock deployment followed the university's centralized security-video access-control regime?
data.method: Reused the landed #1900 Cornell records, searched the corpus for the Cornell security standard/NVSSO terminology, then reconciled current Policy 8.1 with Cornell Design and Construction Standard 281316 without promoting general university requirements into Flock-specific implementation facts.
data.framework: Policy authority, design/commissioning requirements, actual platform integration, exemptions, credentials, configuration, retention, sharing, and observed activity remain separate predicates.
data.scope: Public institutional controls for Cornell's reported campus Flock deployment; no private-person enrichment.
findings: Current Cornell Policy 8.1 requires cameras to be integrated into the university centralized security-video system unless an exemption is granted, with visibility to the Division of Public Safety Communications Center, CUPD, and the Access Control Program.

Cornell Design and Construction Standard 281316 states that Access Control Program setup for camera work includes configuration and labeling, device hardening, user/password configuration, and creation of the device instance in the video-management software.

The same standard states that the building/unit Network Video Surveillance System Operator approves camera views after commissioning and that local-management access is not granted until training plus authorization and activation forms are completed.

These institutional requirements create a concrete Flock-specific evidence request but do not prove that the reported seven Flock readers were integrated, exempted, or administered by any particular person.
conclusions: Request #1900 can now seek a bounded native implementation package rather than only generic policy: Flock integration/exemption record, authorization/activation forms, NVSSO designation/training, commissioning records, VMS device instances, and Access Control Program configuration records.
No Flock user/admin identity, camera identity, sharing edge, configured-retention value, or actual query is created from the general Cornell standard.
recommendations: Recover the Flock-specific Policy 8.1 integration or exemption decision and any related unit security plan.
Recover authorization/activation forms, NVSSO designation/training records, commissioning records, and any centralized VMS device instances specifically tied to the seven Flock readers.
Join those records to native Flock users/admins, Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks, retention-change history, and deletion evidence before asserting implementation or access.
counterarguments: The 2023 construction standard may govern a different installation class or architecture than the reported Flock deployment; that applicability must be proven rather than assumed.
Policy 8.1's centralized-integration rule can coexist with an exemption, so absence from the central VMS would not by itself prove noncompliance.
limitations: No executed Flock contract, invoice, camera serial inventory, Flock configuration export, Cornell exemption record, authorization/activation form, NVSSO roster, or commissioning record was recovered in this pass.
unresolved: Were the seven Flock readers integrated into Cornell's centralized security-video system, exempted, or governed by another implementation path?
Which authorization/activation, training, commissioning, and VMS records exist for the deployment?
Who actually held Flock credentials and what permissions, sharing edges, retention values, and audit activity existed?
